hints: Read the stress at the given strain from the straight-line graph, remembering that the vertical axis is in GPa.
The force is the stress multiplied by the circular cross-sectional area of the wire, using radius equal to half the stated diameter.
walkthrough: At strain 5.4 × 10⁻³, the graph gives a stress of 0.72 GPa = 0.72 × 10⁹ Pa.
The wire radius is r = (1.2 × 10⁻³)/2 = 0.60 × 10⁻³ m, so its cross-sectional area is A = πr² = π(0.60 × 10⁻³)² = 1.13 × 10⁻⁶ m².
Use stress = force / area, so F = σA.
To two significant figures, the force exerted on the wire is 810 N.

ai_rubric.observable: Either reads the stress as 0.72 × 10⁹ Pa, or determines the Young modulus from the graph gradient as about 1.33 × 10¹¹ Pa.
Uses the circular area π(1.2 × 10⁻³/2)² m² with either F = σA or F = EεA.
Obtains the force on the wire as 810 N.

hints: Use the force obtained in part (i) with the elastic-energy relationship to find the extension of the wire.
Once the extension is known, relate it to the given strain to recover the original length.
walkthrough: The wire obeys Hooke's law, so its elastic potential energy is Eₚ = ½Fx.
Using the force from part (i), rearrange to x = 2Eₚ/F = (2 × 0.31)/810 = 7.65 × 10⁻⁴ m.
Strain is ε = x/L, so the original length is L = x/ε.
To two significant figures, the wire's original length is 0.14 m.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses an accepted elastic-energy relationship, either Eₚ = ½Fx or Eₚ = ½kx² with the Young-modulus relation for k.
Obtains an extension of approximately 7.7 × 10⁻⁴ m using either accepted route.
Uses L = x/ε to obtain an original wire length of 0.14 m.

hints: For a wire obeying Hooke's law, the stress–strain graph is a straight line through the origin and its gradient is the Young modulus.
Wire Y has twice the Young modulus of X, so use a line with twice the steepness of X on the same axes.
walkthrough: For a wire in the proportional region, Young modulus is stress divided by strain, so it is the gradient of a stress–strain graph.
Because Y obeys Hooke's law, its graph is a straight line that passes through the origin.
Y has twice the Young modulus of X, so the gradient of Y's line must be twice the gradient of X's line.
Draw a straight line from the origin that is twice as steep as X; it reaches 1.0 GPa at a strain of about 3.75 × 10⁻³.

ai_rubric.observable: Draws a straight line through the origin with a gradient greater than the line for X.
Draws the line with twice the gradient of X, reaching 1.0 GPa at about 3.75 × 10⁻³ strain.
